correctness.rationale: After a first positive query v, a distinct second positive query w leaves q−2 centers on one coordinate line at distance one, exactly two intermediate centers at distance two, and none beyond that. On a coordinate line a query on the line excludes at most one center; a query off the line includes at most one. Thus every genuine second split has a branch of Littlestone dimension ≤1, the first-positive space has dimension ≤2, and the full dimension is ≤3. In dimension one a negative answer identifies the center; H(2,2) has only two distinct concepts, and in H(3,2) the first-positive space has only three centers and hence cannot realize depth two. The independent replay `python3 /workspace/review-evidence/independent_finite_checks.py 5` verified every frozen certificate path under distance-one labels, giving depths 3,3,2 in H(2,3), H(4,2), H(3,2), respectively. Fixing extra coordinates and restricting symbols preserves all these labels, giving the lower bounds for larger graphs. Independently, no triple in H(2,3) can be VC-shattered: a distance-one pair has only one common neighbor, and a triple of pairwise distance-two points can be relabeled as the diagonal, which has no common neighbor. Two points are shattered. Standard version-space prediction and the shattered-tree adversary identify the dimension with the deterministic realizable mistake bound.
